failure_modes: no storage -> throws, refuses to operate blind
createInvite without a peerId -> throws; a code identifying nobody pairs nobody
createInvite while paired -> throws, names the partner
scanning an expired code -> throws, says to ask for a fresh one
receiveRequest on a used/expired/mismatched code -> refused with the reason named
emailInvite before an invite exists -> throws
invariants: SOLO IS THE DEFAULT and a complete mode. No partner account is seeded — one exists only when a real person accepts.
the invite prompt appears ONCE. 'I'm riding solo' and 'skip' both silence it permanently; pairing stays available in Settings.
SCANNING DOES NOT PAIR — it creates a request the issuing side confirms. Same shape as the grammar store.
codes are SINGLE-USE and EXPIRE (24h default). A pairing link that works forever is a permanent open door on whatever it passed through.
the payload carries no name, no password, nothing about the person — a code photographed off a screen reveals nothing
unpair is unilateral. Nobody needs permission to be solo.
§1.2 a weak randomness source is reported in health(), never assumed away
§1.2 a peerId containing the account key is flagged as an identity leak
found_by_test: The payload test caught a REAL leak, not a fixture artifact: peer ids were minted as `eravos-<account key>-fixed`, so every pairing code announced who made it. Fixed at the source with opaque ids; the detector stays so the next one is named too.
